correctness.rationale: Strict inequality T(n)<=16k<3^(k-1)<=n for every k-digit n with k>=5 implies all orbits enter 1..80. All possible digit counts for at most four ternary digits have exactly 14 distinct images, whose full 14-arrow graph closes and has precisely the three stated cycles. The digitwise congruence d^4=d (mod 2) proves parity preservation. Actual standalone checker recomputed all edges and independently checked 1..80; no infinite inference relies on finite experimentation.

originality.rationale: The explicit complete ternary quartic cycle set, exact fourteen-state closed graph, and parity-separated basins are not stated by the three inspected primary works, which establish a general finite-cycle algorithm, base-three parity invariance, or tree methods. The result is a new exact natural instance under the accessible published evidence, not a claim to invent the general algorithm. Literature/index incompleteness remains a risk.
residual_risks: The 2021/2022 comprehensive survey could not be inspected in full; its body may contain a preexisting exact (4,3) table.

The result is an explicitly evaluated low-parameter case of an existing algorithm, not a new general dynamical theorem.

value.rationale: The problem asks for a natural, exact global phase portrait of the smallest nonbinary positional digit-power system beyond the previously tabulated square/cube exponents. A complete classification of periodic points and parity-separated attraction basins is an invariant that structures all generalized happy and unhappy numbers of this pair, and is needed before studying heights or densities. It is a finite but globally exhaustive answer, with transparent proof that does not assume a search cutoff; its modest computational complexity and previous general algorithms are explicit limitations, not claimed innovations.
